failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 states 'The passages identify K. Shivaram Karanth as the author of "Marali Mannige" (Passage [1]), but provide no information about whether K. Shivaram Karanth is or was a Yakshagana artist.' However, the passages available at hop 1 already included passage [2] about K. Shivaram Karanth stating 'Kota Shivaram Karanth (10 October 1902 – 9 December 1997) was a Kannada writer, social activist, environmentalist, Yakshagana artist, film maker and thinker.' This information was present but the solver at hop 1 missed it.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Query at hop 2 asks 'What is the professional background and career of K. Shivaram Karanth, including whether he is or was involved in Yakshagana performance?' Query at hop 3 asks 'Was K. Shivaram Karanth a Yakshagana artist, and in what year was the novel Marali Mannige published?' Both queries target the same core information about K. Shivaram Karanth being a Yakshagana artist, which was already answered in hop 2 retrieval results. The queries fail to advance meaningfully despite hop 2 already retrieving the K. Shivaram Karanth passage confirming he was a Yakshagana artist.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: (i) Summary_1 explicitly names the missing information: 'Publication Date of Marali Mannige: While Passage [1] confirms K. Shivaram Karanth wrote "Marali Mannige," it does not provide the publication year. Verification that "Marali Mannige" was specifically published in 2000 is required.' (ii) Query at hop 3 targets this gap: 'Was K. Shivaram Karanth a Yakshagana artist, and in what year was the novel Marali Mannige published?' Despite this well-formed query, no passage across any hop provides the publication year of Marali Mannige, indicating a corpus gap.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: At hop 1, the solver extensively analyzes passages [5] (Costume designer), [6] (List of Yakshagana artists - generic), and [7] (Conor O'Sullivan make-up artist) which are clearly irrelevant to verifying whether K. Shivaram Karanth is a Yakshagana artist or the publication date of Marali Mannige. These passages receive attention in the reasoning despite being tangential to the claim.
